title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Maya Singh
description:
Context: Continuous batching reduces per-token cost and amortizes GPU work, but production can see unfair queueing (large / long requests starving short requests), occasional starvation during bursty workloads, and difficulty enforcing per-request timeouts which hurt latency SLOs. This PR implements a set of scheduler and KV-cache-touching changes to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and reliably enforce timeouts across the continuous-batcher runtime.

What I changed: 1) Scheduler aging & weighted fairness: introduce a lightweight priority aging mechanism that incrementally increases effective priority for requests waiting beyond a configurable threshold. This prevents starvation of low-priority/short requests when the system is dominated by long-running high-priority batches. We combine aging with a tenant-aware weighted round-robin policy so guaranteed-capacity tenants still receive expected share. 2) Queueing isolation: split the continuous-batcher queue into short/long lanes based on estimated compute cost (token estimate + model profile), with a fast-path for sub-128-token requests. Short-lane requests are allowed conservative bypass when utilization < 85% to preserve latency SLOs. 3) Timeout propagation & enforcement: unify client-side deadline propagation and server-side enforcement. Added pre-execution deadline checks in the scheduler loop and a graceful cancellation path that flushes partial metrics and KV-cache touches. 4) KV cache touch semantics: avoid unnecessary KV-cache writes for requests that are likely to be aborted early; add a 'touch-on-commit' toggle and instrumentation to track cache hit-rate impact. 5) Monitoring & telemetry: new queue-level metrics (lane_wait_time_seconds, aged_request_count, starvation_incidents_total), and dashboards/alerts for queue tail latency and starvation. 6) Tests & canary plan: comprehensive unit/integration tests plus a staged canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback criteria tied to P95 latency regressions and starvation_incidents_total.

Why this approach: previous heuristics improved throughput at cost of occasional P99 latency spikes under bursty multi-tenant workloads. The combined aging + lane isolation preserves high throughput while bounding tail latency and preventing pathological starvation. Timeout enforcement avoids wasted GPU execution and improves signal for upstream backpressure.

Results: In internal stress tests (multi-tenant, mixed short/long traffic) we saw: - P50 latency: unchanged (-2ms) - P95 latency: -18ms on average for short requests - P99 latency: -85ms for short requests under mixed load - Overall throughput: +3% for 1k token-equivalent workload - Starvation incidents (simulated long-tail cases): reduced from 12/hour to 0 in 6h long-run tests.

Migration notes and config: New runtime config keys (continuous_batcher.scheduler.max_age_ms, continuous_batcher.scheduler.short_lane_token_cutoff, continuous_batcher.scheduler.short_lane_bypass_util_pct, continuous_batcher.kv.touch_on_commit). Defaults chosen for conservative safety; canary rollout will tune for each cluster.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler logic + unit tests - [x] Integration tests with simulated multi-tenant traffic - [x] Add metrics, dashboards, alert rules - [x] Update docs: docs/ops/continuous-batcher.md - [x] Canary plan in Linear ENG-3421

Related: ENG-3421 (scheduler tuning), ENG-3480 (kv-cache instrumentation), previous PRs: pr-41213, pr-53984.
